subject: Dedicated capacity recap - Helix Health
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thompson <sara@helixhealth.com>; Alex Jones <alex.jones@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap - Helix Health

Hi Sara / Alex -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Pain points you called out:
- Unpredictable latency and tail spikes during peak booking windows (esp. model chat + reranking).
- Need for strict data isolation / compliance for PHI-adjacent workloads.
- Cost predictability: you want fixed committed spend for peak months, avoid large overage surprises.

Goals we heard:
- Pilot dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) to remove noisy-neighbor variance.
- Meet 95th percentile latency < 120ms for inference paths in production, while supporting burst capacity during spikes.
- Full compliance evidence (SOC 2 + KMS keys + VPC peering) for procurement.

What we propose / discussed on call:
- Dedicated cluster with reserved nodes (2 x A100 equivalent to start) + burst pool for spikes.
- Autoscaling policy tuned for rapid scale-up on queue depth with warm KV cache to reduce cold-starts.
- Network-level isolation via VPC peering and dedicated storage volumes; optional on-prem/private control plane if required.
- SLA target: 99.95% uptime for dedicated cluster + latency SLOs we can target by route (we'll propose specific SLOs in SOW).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-capacity-plan-helix-v1.xlsx (capacity + scaling plan), redwood-sow-dedicated-helix-v1.pdf (draft SOW).

Next steps:
1) I attached the capacity plan + draft SOW - please review with procurement/security.
2) Technical deep-dive: Rishi (cc'd) to run an architecture session with your infra/sre team - can we target next Wed or Thu?
3) Procurement: Ben to follow up on pricing/term questions and add commercial options (reserved monthly commit vs. annual).

If that matches your notes, can you confirm internal timeline (procurement/PO target date) and whether Alex should take the security deep-dive from your side?

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap - Helix Health

Thanks Ben - useful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: we ran some internal numbers and our peak inference volume is ~3.5k concurrent requests (tails up to ~6k during promotions); average tokens per request ~600. Our internal SRE priority is to keep 95th pctl latency <= 120ms as you noted.

Security/compliance: SOC 2 evidence is essential; we also need confirmation that encryption at rest is customer-managed (KMS) and audit logs for admin actions. Alex (cc) is our security lead - Alex, would you be the right person for the technical deep-dive?

Procurement timeline: target to have PO / decision by 2027-05-20, ideally sooner if we can lock pricing.

I'll take a look through the attachments and loop in procurement.

- Sara
Director of Platform Engineering | Helix Health
sara@helixhealth.com

Appreciate the data points, Sara - super helpful. Quick answers: 
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II for our hosted control plane; for Dedicated we can provide scoped evidence and support for your auditor.
- KMS / encryption at rest: yes - Customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; keys can be provisioned via your cloud KMS/HSM and we do not hold plaintext keys.
- Audit logs: Admin actions, rollouts, and key events are available via our audit logging (retention configurable as part of the premium observability add-on).

On sizing: starting with 2 x A100-like nodes should handle baseline with autoscale to an additional 2 nodes for bursts; Rishi can validate simulator numbers against your request profile in the deep-dive. We will also include a warm-cache strategy in the runbook to keep latency stable during spikes.

SLA: For Dedicated customers we offer a targeted uptime SLA of 99.95% for the reserved cluster and per-route latency SLOs; we can discuss financial credit terms in commercial paperwork.

Next from us: Rishi - can you run the deep-dive and share a short sim report and a recommended autoscale policy? Marissa - I'll coordinate commercial options and timeline.

Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Looping in a couple things from ops/onboarding perspective:
- We can support a staged onboarding: pilot (2 reserved nodes) -> scale to target capacity after a 2-week soak test. During pilot we provide a dedicated onboarding SRE contact and a runbook for warm cache + scaling checklists.
- Documentation: attaching a slightly updated SOW that flags the SOC2 evidence and the KMS integration steps.
- Timeline: if procurement aims for 2027-05-20, we should target contract signing by 2027-05-10 to allow a 2-week procurement lead time for legal/PO.

Rishi - happy to have you lead the technical deep-dive; please propose 30-45 minute slots tomorrow/Wednesday and include the simulator outputs.

Thanks - Marissa
